question.value: Investigate the physical and chemical conditions (rotational temperatures, column densities, abundances, chemical differentiation, and COM formation routes) of dense cores at different evolutionary stages in G9.62+0.19.

evidence.quote: Here we preform a detailed analysis of the physical and chemical conditions (e.g., temperature, density, and possible chemical formation routes of COMs) of dense cores in G9.62+0.19 through ALMA band 3 observations.
G9.62+0.19 was observed with ALMA in band 3 (Project ID: 2019.1.00685.S; PI: Tie Liu), as part of the ATOMS survey, which was conducted towards 146 IRAS clumps (cite: Liu20a; Liu20b; Liu2021).
This paper makes use of the following ALMA data: ADS/JAO.ALMA#2019.1.00685.S.
We performed a detailed line survey toward six dense cores named as MM1, MM4, MM6, MM7, MM8, and MM11 in G9.62+0.19 star-forming region resolved in ALMA band 3 observations.
Figure 1 shows the 3 mm continuum emission of G9.62+0.19 observed by the 12-m array alone and 12-m+ACA combined data.

analysis_steps.goal: Derive rotational temperatures, column densities, and line optical depths via LTE spectral modeling

method.value: Model observed 12-m spectra using myXCLASS and MAGIX under LTE assumptions, fitting unblended transitions (>3 transitions with wide Eu range) for T_rot and N_T, or fixing T_rot to core average gas temperature when fewer than 3 transitions are detected.

evidence.quote: The software includes myXCLASS program, which is used to model data by solving the radiative transfer equation.

We model the observed spectra using the XCLASS suite. The software contains an interface for the model optimizer package MAGIX (Modeling and Analysis Generic Interface for eXternal numerical codes; (cite: Moller13)), which helps to optimize the fit, finds the best solutions of parameters, and provides corresponding error estimates by using different optimization algorithms or algorithm chain.

fitting.value: Chi-squared minimization in MAGIX using Genetic, Levenberg-Marquardt, and Markov chain Monte Carlo (MCMC) algorithms; 1D Gaussian fits for velocity offsets and line widths.

evidence.quote: In this work, three algorithm including Genetic, Levenberg–Marquardt, and Markov chain Monte Carlo were adopted.

The velocity offsets and line widths are derived from Gaussian fits to the spectral lines. The rest of the parameters are set as free parameters, mainly the rotational temperature and column density. Then MAGIX is used to minimizes the $\chi^{2}$ in the given parameter space.

findings_qualitative.value: About 172 transitions attributed to 16 molecular species (including O-, N-, and S-bearing molecules and isotopologues) are identified toward six dense cores in G9.62+0.19, with MM7, MM8, MM4, and MM11 being line-rich.

evidence.quote: Toward these cores, about 172 transitions have been identified and attributed to 16 species including organic Oxygen-, Nitrogen-, Sulfur-bearing molecules and their isotopologues. Four dense cores MM7, MM8, MM4, and MM11 are line rich sources.

findings_qualitative.value: The evolutionary sequence of the six dense cores is classified as MM6 (HMPO) -> MM7 (early HMC) -> MM8 (HMC) -> MM4 (evolved HMC) -> MM11 (HMC/UC HII) -> MM1 (evolved HII), while MM3 and MM9 are massive starless core candidates.

evidence.quote: MM3 and MM9 are considered as massive starless core candidates.
In short, their evolutionary sequence is MM6$\rightarrow$MM7$\rightarrow$MM8$\rightarrow$MM4$\rightarrow$MM11$\rightarrow$MM1.

findings_qualitative.value: MM4 and MM8 exhibit strong N/O chemical differentiation: MM4 dominates in O-bearing COMs while MM8 dominates in N-bearing (especially C2H5CN and vibrationally excited HC3N) and S-bearing molecules.

evidence.quote: The cores MM8 and MM4 show chemical difference between Oxygen- and Nitrogen-bearing species, i.e., MM4 is rich in oxygen-bearing molecules while nitrogen-bearing molecules especially vibrationally excited HC$_{3}$N lines are mainly observed in MM8.
The emission of N-bearing and S-bearing molecules is strongest toward MM8, while emission of O-bearings is dominated by core MM4.

findings_qualitative.value: Spatial distributions and column density correlations indicate that C2H5OH and CH3OCH3 likely share CH3OH as a common precursor, and CH3OCHO and CH3OCH3 are chemically linked, whereas chemical links within the C2HnO family (H2CCO, CH3CHO, C2H5OH) remain uncertain.

evidence.quote: Through analyzing column densities and spatial distributions of O-bearing Complex Organic Molecules (COMs), we found that C$_{2}$H$_{5}$OH and CH$_{3}$OCH$_{3}$ might have a common precursor, CH$_{3}$OH. CH$_{3}$OCHO and CH$_{3}$OCH$_{3}$ are likely chemically linked.
It seems likely that the chemical link of O-bearing COMs in the formula C$_{2}$H$_{\rm n}$O is uncertain at present work.

findings_qualitative.value: HC5N spatial distribution differs from HC3N and its isotopologues/vibrationally excited states, suggesting different formation mechanisms in hot and cold regions, while C2H5CN is spatially correlated with HC3N.

evidence.quote: is almost identical to that of HC$_{3}$N, predicting that C$_{2}$H$_{5}$CN is correlated with HC$_{3}$N in formation mechanism
The comparison of HC$_{3}$N and HC$_{5}$N suggests that they trace different gas structures, and the formation mechanisms of HC$_{3}$N and HC$_{5}$N may differ in hot and cold regions.

claims.hypothesis: Molecular abundances and temperatures of massive dense cores vary systematically along their evolutionary sequence.
claims.experiment: Classify six dense cores in G9.62+0.19 by molecular richness, high-Eu states, outflows, and recombination lines, and fit LTE rotational temperatures and abundances across the sequence MM7 -> MM8 -> MM4 -> MM11.
claims.result: Mean rotational temperatures are 99 K (MM7), 134 K (MM8), 137 K (MM4), and 100 K (MM11); mean COM abundances increase from 3.0x10^-8 (MM7) to 1.0x10^-7 (MM8) and 6.9x10^-7 (MM4), then drop to 7.4x10^-8 in MM11.
claims.finding: Molecular abundance increases with core evolutionary age during the hot core phase and decreases at the UC HII phase (MM11) due to UV destruction.

evidence.quote: The mean values of the two parameters are: $T_{\rm rot}$ = 99$\pm$28 K, $\chi$= (3.0$\pm$1.2)$\times$10$^{-8}$ for MM7, $T_{\rm rot}$ = 134$\pm$27 K, $\chi$= (1.0$\pm$0.2)$\times$10$^{-7}$ for MM8, $T_{\rm rot}$ = 137$\pm$21 K, $\chi$= (6.9$\pm$1.7)$\times$10$^{-7}$ for MM4, and $T_{\rm rot}$ = 100$\pm$18 K, $\chi$= (7.4$\pm$2.6)$\times$10$^{-8}$ for MM11.
In brief, molecular abundance increases with increasing age, except in the last phase MM11 which shows a decrease in abundance probably due to the destruction of molecules by the UV radiation.

claims.hypothesis: Hot cores MM4 and MM8 in G9.62+0.19 exhibit chemical differentiation between O-bearing and N-bearing species driven by different initial accretion temperatures.
claims.experiment: Compare integrated intensity maps, line detections, and LTE abundances of O-bearing and N-bearing species toward MM4 and MM8.
claims.result: O-bearing COMs (CH3OH, CH3OCHO, C2H5OH, CH3OCH3) peak and have highest abundances at MM4, while N-bearing species (C2H5CN, vibrationally excited HC3N up to v6=1) peak and have highest abundances at MM8 (e.g., C2H5CN abundance 9.0x10^-8 in MM8 vs 1.3x10^-8 in MM4).
claims.finding: Clear N/O chemical differentiation exists between MM8 and MM4, likely caused by external heating of MM8 by nearby HII region B during the gravitational collapse/accretion phase.

evidence.loc: Discussions / Chemical differentiation / Chemical Differentiation between Nitrogen-bearing and Oxygen-bearing species
evidence.quote: The derived abundances shows that MM4 is an O-rich source, while MM8 is rich in N-bearing species.

evidence.loc: Discussions / Chemical differentiation / Chemical Differentiation between Nitrogen-bearing and Oxygen-bearing species
evidence.quote: Considering that the MM8 region could be externally heated at the gravitationally collapse phase due to its proximity to H II "B", its initial temperature at accretion phase is likely to be higher than that of MM4.

claims.hypothesis: O-bearing COMs C2H5OH, CH3OCH3, and CH3OCHO are chemically linked and share CH3OH (or CH3O) as a common precursor.
claims.experiment: Analyze spatial distributions and column density / abundance correlations among CH3OH, C2H5OH, CH3OCH3, and CH3OCHO across G9.62+0.19 cores and literature HMSFR/LMSFR/GCMC sources.
claims.result: Positive correlations are found for CH3OH/C2H5OH, CH3OH/CH3OCH3, and CH3OCHO/CH3OCH3 with similar spatial distributions across MM4, MM7, MM8, and MM11, and CH3OCHO/CH3OCH3 ratios of 0.6 to 2.0.
claims.finding: C2H5OH and CH3OCH3 likely share CH3OH as a common precursor, and CH3OCHO and CH3OCH3 are chemically linked.

evidence.loc: Discussions / Chemical differentiation / Chemical relationships of Oxygen-bearing molecules
evidence.quote: The spatial distributions of CH$_{3}$OH, CH$_{3}$OCH$_{3}$, and C$_{2}$H$_{5}$OH that are mainly shown toward the MM4, MM7, MM8, and MM11, suggest that C$_{2}$H$_{5}$OH and CH$_{3}$OCH$_{3}$ might have a common precursor, CH$_{3}$OH.

We found tight correlations between the column density of molecular pairs CH$_{3}$OH/C$_{2}$H$_{5}$OH, CH$_{3}$OH/CH$_{3}$OCH$_{3}$, and CH$_{3}$OCHO/CH$_{3}$OCH$_{3}$. Furthermore, the similar spatial distribution between them is seen, indicating that each pair is likely chemically linked, and may share a common precursor.

claims.hypothesis: COMs with formula C2HnO (H2CCO, CH3CHO, C2H5OH) are chemically linked via successive grain-surface hydrogenation.
claims.experiment: Compare spatial distributions and column density/abundance correlations of H2CCO, CH3CHO, C2H5OH, and CH3OCH3 in G9.62+0.19 and literature sources.
claims.result: No clear correlation is found between H2CCO and other C2HnO molecules in G9.62+0.19, and CH3CHO emission extends to the east unlike H2CCO and C2H5OH.
claims.finding: The predicted chemical link among C2HnO family molecules is challenged and cannot be confirmed.

evidence.loc: Discussions / Chemical differentiation / Chemical relationships of Oxygen-bearing molecules
evidence.quote: The correlation plots (see Figure 5) for each pair of H$_{2}$CCO/CH$_{3}$CHO, H$_{2}$CCO/C$_{2}$H$_{5}$OH, and H$_{2}$CCO/CH$_{3}$OCH$_{3}$ showed that there is no clear relationship between H$_{2}$CCO and other C$_{2}$H$_{\rm n}$O group molecules.

evidence.loc: Discussions / Chemical differentiation / Chemical relationships of Oxygen-bearing molecules
evidence.quote: These results challenge the prediction that COMs in the formula of C$_{2}$H$_{\rm n}$O have chemical correlation.

claims.hypothesis: HC5N and HC3N share the same formation pathway in massive star-forming regions.
claims.experiment: Compare integrated intensity distributions and line intensity ratios of HC5N and HC3N across the cores in G9.62+0.19.
claims.result: HC3N and its isotopologues/vibrational states peak on the continuum cores (matching C2H5CN), whereas HC5N is offset from continuum peaks MM4 and MM7 and has a MM3/MM4 intensity ratio of ~1.3 compared to ~0.5 for HC3N.
claims.finding: HC5N is not simply generated from HC3N; HC3N and HC5N trace different gas structures and have different formation mechanisms in hot and cold regions.

evidence.loc: Discussions / Chemical differentiation / Chemical relationships of Nitrogen-bearing molecules
evidence.quote: However, the distribution of HC$_{5}$N has its own unique characteristics which differ from the distributions of HC$_{3}$N. Therefore, it seems that HC$_{5}$N is not generated from HC$_{3}$N.
The comparison of HC$_{3}$N and HC$_{5}$N suggests that they trace different gas structures, and the formation mechanisms of HC$_{3}$N and HC$_{5}$N may differ in hot and cold regions.

why_this_data.value: G9.62+0.19 contains dense cores spanning multiple evolutionary stages and rich chemistry, making ALMA Band 3 observations from the ATOMS survey ideal for exploring chemical differentiation; 12-m array data alone are used for line modeling because they provide higher angular resolution for compact cores without suffering missing flux on <10'' scales, while 1.3 mm archival continuum is used for H2 column densities to avoid 3 mm free-free contamination.

evidence.quote: In general, G9.62+0.19 contains different evolutionary types of dense cores, and harbours rich chemistry indicating that it is an ideal object to explore the distinct chemical properties of cores at different evolutionary stages.

However, at 3 mm observations, free-free emission from ionized gas could contribute to the continuum emission (detailed analyses are provided in (cite: Liu20a; Liu2021)), which will overestimate the column density of H$_{2}$. Instead, we use 1.3 mm continuum data from (cite: Liu17), and smooth it to the same spatial resolution as that of 3 mm continuum data.

evidence.loc: Spectra from 12-m array and 12-m + ACA combined data.
evidence.quote: Therefore, 12-m array and combined data have no difference when using them to study the hot core chemistry, but 12-m array data have higher angular resolution for better investigating the compact cores.

why_this_method.value: XCLASS with MAGIX solves the radiative transfer equation under LTE while accounting for beam dilution, dust attenuation, line opacity, and line blending; abundances relative to CH3OH are used when comparing with literature sources to mitigate differences in spatial resolution and spectral setup across telescopes.

evidence.quote: Under the assumption of local thermodynamical equilibrium (LTE), XCLASS takes the beam dilution, dust attenuation, the line opacity, and line blending into account (cite: Moller17).

evidence.loc: Discussions / Chemical differentiation / Chemical relationships of Oxygen-bearing molecules
evidence.quote: Since column densities of these O-bearing COMs have been derived from various observational equipments with different spatial resolution and spectral setup, comparison of column density is not very helpful to derive sound conclusions for chemical links among O-bearing COMs. It is more reliable to compare the abundance of COMs relative to CH$_{3}$OH.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Using 3 mm continuum emission to derive H2 column densities was rejected because free-free emission from ionized gas at 3 mm would overestimate N_H2; 1.3 mm continuum from Liu et al. (2017) was used instead.

evidence.quote: However, at 3 mm observations, free-free emission from ionized gas could contribute to the continuum emission (detailed analyses are provided in (cite: Liu20a; Liu2021)), which will overestimate the column density of H$_{2}$. Instead, we use 1.3 mm continuum data from (cite: Liu17), and smooth it to the same spatial resolution as that of 3 mm continuum data.

alternatives_considered_or_rejected.value: Using 12-m+ACA combined spectra for hot core LTE modeling was tested and rejected in favor of 12-m array alone to retain higher angular resolution for the compact cores.

evidence.loc: Spectra from 12-m array and 12-m + ACA combined data.
evidence.quote: Therefore, 12-m array and combined data have no difference when using them to study the hot core chemistry, but 12-m array data have higher angular resolution for better investigating the compact cores.

limitations_admitted.value: 12-m array observations are affected by missing flux (~5% of extended continuum emission missed compared to 12-m+ACA, and HC3N v=0 / 13C isotopologue ratios underestimated by a factor of six due to large optical depth and possible missing flux).

evidence.quote: The observations of 12-m array missed $\sim$ 5% of extended emissions compared to the observations of 12-m + ACA combined data.
The ratios between HC$_{3}$N v=0 and its isotopologues are underestimated by a factor of six, which may due to the large optical depth and possible missing-flux of HC$_{3}$N v=0.

limitations_admitted.value: Cores MM2, MM3, MM5, MM9, and MM10 are not resolved in the 3 mm continuum map due to the relatively lower spatial resolution, and 2D Gaussian fitting toward MM7 failed to converge because it is not well resolved.

evidence.quote: However, these cores are not resolved in 3 mm map possibly because of the relatively lower spatial resolution of our observations.
| $^a$ The 2-D Gaussian fitting toward the MM7 suffered failed convergence due to this core is not well resolved by 3 mm continuum emission. |

limitations_admitted.value: For several molecules in specific cores (e.g., CH3OH in MM7/MM8/MM11, CH3CHO, HC5N, HC13CCN, HCC13CN, CH3OCH3 in MM7, C2H5OH in MM11), fewer than three transitions or insufficient Eu range were detected, requiring T_rot to be fixed to the core average temperature.

evidence.quote: For MM7, three transitions with $E_{\rm u}$ of 10 K are observed. Therefore, its temperatures and densities cannot be calculated due to lack of sufficient $E_{u}$ range.

evidence.loc: LTE Analyses / Rotational Temperatures and Column Densities
evidence.quote: As mentioned above, some molecules (e.g., methanol, acetaldehyde, dimethyl ether, etc) are observed with only one or two detected transitions. In this case, we fix the rotational temperature, then get the column densities for those species.

limitations_admitted.value: Four dense cores in G9.62+0.19 provide a very limited sample size for testing chemical correlations among COMs.

evidence.loc: Discussions / Chemical differentiation / Chemical relationships of Oxygen-bearing molecules
evidence.quote: Moreover, comparisons of the very limited sample can not testify the potential chemical link among species well.

referee_caveats_inferred: Adopting a single core-averaged rotational temperature for species with <3 transitions (including ground-state CH3OH in MM7, MM8, and MM11) ignores temperature gradients and the fact that different species trace different spatial layers.

Deriving H2 column densities from 1.3 mm continuum smoothed to 3 mm resolution (~1.5 arcsec) while fitting molecular source sizes independently in XCLASS can introduce beam-dilution and spatial-scale mismatches in fractional abundances.
Linear/correlation analyses on 4 cores in G9.62+0.19 have very low statistical degrees of freedom.
